title: Common memory mistakes: leaks, double-free, use-after-free and invalid free
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or control flow.
Recognize common failure and safety cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A memory leak occurs when allocated storage becomes unreachable without being released. Double-free releases the same allocation more than once. Use-after-free accesses an object after its lifetime ends. Invalid free passes a pointer that was not returned by a compatible allocation function or has already been released.
understand.whyItMatters: These defects can cause crashes, data corruption and security vulnerabilities. They often arise when ownership is unclear or error paths skip cleanup.
understand.analogy: Treat each resource and operation as having a clear contract, valid lifetime and failure path.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, compiler or library specifications.

explain.narrative:
A memory leak occurs when allocated storage becomes unreachable without being released. Double-free releases the same allocation more than once. Use-after-free accesses an object after its lifetime ends. Invalid free passes a pointer that was not returned by a compatible allocation function or has already been released.

Check object bounds, lifetimes, arithmetic limits and all relevant return values. Compile with warnings enabled and test both normal and failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The example follows one allocation with one release and clears the local owner pointer. It avoids accessing the object after free and avoids freeing the same pointer twice.

practise.guidedTask: For each named defect, describe the incorrect operation and its consequence.
practise.independentTask: Review a function with several early returns and ensure every successful allocation is released exactly once.
hints: Use one clear owner for each allocation whenever possible.
After free, do not use any alias to the released object.
Use sanitizers or memory-checking tools where available, but still reason about ownership.
